note: User-facing acceptance cases for andenken. DATA, not a roadmap — adding a case must never require editing acceptance.ts. Committed content is public-safe by construction: intent, query, and expected EVIDENCE TYPE only. No machine name, no session UUID, no path binding to a private transcript. Volatile bindings live in acceptance-cases.local.json (gitignored), merged over this file by case id and probe id. A case whose local binding is missing or expired reports `abstain` / `expired` — never a suite pass and never a suite failure.

caseTypes.lookup: The steward knows which room they want. Canonical evidence must be reachable from the first screen; a single document dominating top-K is a WARNING, not an automatic failure — a narrow lookup legitimately returns one document.
caseTypes.explore: The steward is surveying. Numeric guardrails (distinct documents, per-document share) are necessary and NOT sufficient: a diverse screen of irrelevant documents is a worse answer than a narrow relevant one. Semantic usefulness is graded by labeled neighbors, and where labels are absent the automated verdict is capped below pass and handed to the steward.
caseTypes.time-probe: A day is asked about. andenken grades only recoverable session/md anchors inside a caller-supplied ISO window, or an honest miss. Zero rows is `honest-miss`, never a retrieval PASS and never an empty day — the timeline skill owns whether the day was lived.

relevanceLabels.canonical: The document the steward was actually after.
relevanceLabels.helpfulNeighbor: A different document that genuinely advances the same question. Must be observed and labeled by a human — never guessed by the runner.
relevanceLabels.knownDistractor: A document observed to crowd the first screen without advancing the question. If one ranks ahead of canonical the run is at most `partial`.

cases.title: Something decided an hour ago is retrievable after sync
cases.userQuestion: 방금 전 디스크 꽉 찼던 빌드 캐시 사건, 어떻게 처리하기로 했지?
cases.why: The most common real failure is not bad ranking — it is asking about something the index has not seen yet. The report must separate 'the index is behind' from 'ranking failed', because the operator fix is completely different: run a sync, versus change the ranker. The freshness warning must be read BEFORE any ranking interpretation.
cases.evidenceType: A session transcript written today in a personal-repo project, still being appended to.
cases.bindingHint: Bind `freshnessAnchors` and `probes[].evidence.canonical` in acceptance-cases.local.json. Rebind the anchor and the query together when the incident ages out; do not keep grading a months-old transcript as 'recent'.

ownership.timeline: Owns whether the incident happened and at which KST coordinate.
ownership.andenken: Grades only whether the session anchor is recoverable, or reports index-freshness / corpus miss honestly.
ownership.harness: Grades whether the recovered evidence restores the decision and the next move.

probes.query: zig 빌드 캐시가 디스크를 다 먹었는데 어떻게 정리하기로 했지

cases.humanPrompt: Could you choose or reject the right session from this first screen, without re-querying?
cases.harnessGrades: Did the answer name the decision and the reason, not merely surface the transcript?

cases.title: A natural-language question with no title reaches the canonical note
cases.userQuestion: 내가 지식그래프를 왜 계속 묻는지 정리해 둔 글, 그거 어디 있지?
cases.why: The steward asks in their own words, not by title. If the canonical note is only reachable by exact-title search, retrieval added nothing — the win is measured as one fewer exact-title lookup.

ownership.timeline: Owns nothing here — this is a meaning question with no time claim.
ownership.andenken: Owns the rank of the canonical note under a no-title query.
ownership.harness: Owns whether the steward could act from the first screen.

probes.query: 새 원석을 기존 autholog 방에 넣고 싶다. 흩어진 메모를 서로 연결하면서 내가 계속 전체 지식의 지도를 만들려는 이유를 설명해 둔 방을 찾아줘
probes.queryProvenance: A real steward task phrased as the task, not as the note. An earlier version of this probe repeated the canonical title almost verbatim, which made a rank-1 result meaningless — it was measuring string overlap, not retrieval. `forbiddenQueryTokens` lists the canonical title and subtitle wording, and a fixture test fails if any of it reappears in the query.
probes.labelNote: Labels come from an observed production run through the pi tools, not from the CLI and not from guessing. 20241206T090648 ranked 2 and gave useful scope/magnet context but is not a candidate room, so it is deliberately labeled NEITHER helpful-neighbor nor distractor — mislabeling it either way would corrupt the grade.

cases.humanPrompt: Could you choose or reject an existing room from this first screen?
cases.harnessGrades: One fewer step than before — no re-query, no exact-title search, no extra file open?

cases.title: A survey question returns several genuinely different, genuinely useful notes
cases.userQuestion: 일일일생 관련해서 내가 써 둔 글들 훑어보고 싶다
cases.why: Raw chunk count is not a user effect; documents are. A top-5 filled by one note's adjacent chunks is a five-row screen carrying one document. But diversity alone is equally hollow — five unrelated documents is a worse screen than two relevant ones. Numbers guard the floor; the steward judges usefulness.

ownership.andenken: Owns document-level diversity and the rank of the canonical note.
ownership.harness: Owns whether the returned set is enough to write from.

probes.labelNote: Labels come from a human who read an observed production run through the pi tools (top5: 4 unique documents, max 2 chunks per document). They are not derived from the CLI and not guessed — a guessed label would make this case grade itself.

cases.humanPrompt: From this first screen, could you open 3+ genuinely different notes worth reading — not just 3 different filenames?
cases.harnessGrades: Did the set support writing without a second query?

cases.title: Sessions and garden answer together, labeled — never merged by score
cases.userQuestion: 피투성 개념, 세션에서 얘기한 것도 가든에 쓴 것도 둘 다 보여줘
cases.why: The two tracks emit numbers that are incomparable by construction — different fusion strategies over different distributions. Any single ranking across them is meaningless, and folding private session text into 'garden knowledge' misrepresents what is published. Grade attribution and grouping; compute no merged ranking at all.

ownership.andenken: Owns that each result is attributed to its track with its visibility, and that no cross-track score comparison is emitted.
ownership.harness: Owns whether the composed answer keeps the private/public distinction in what it says back.

cases.humanPrompt: Is it obvious, without opening anything, which rows are private session text and which are published notes?
cases.harnessGrades: Did the answer say which claims come from a private session and which from a published note?

cases.title: A lived day with only depth-0 residue is an honest miss, never an empty day
cases.why: The timeline golden day 2026-02-07 has depth-0 evidence only. andenken must either recover a session/md anchor or report an honest miss. Reporting 'nothing found' as 'nothing happened' is the failure this case exists to make impossible.

ownership.timeline: Owns the coordinate and the source status — empty / partial / stale / unreadable are four different states, not zero.
ownership.andenken: Grades only recoverable session/md anchors inside the supplied ISO window, or an honest miss.
ownership.harness: Grades the synthesis and the next move.

probes.windowNote: KST 2026-02-07 00:00–24:00 expressed as UTC. andenken does not parse natural-language time; the caller supplies ISO. Stored-signal scan — no embedding call, API 0.

cases.humanPrompt: Does this output make it impossible to conclude 'nothing happened that day'?
cases.harnessGrades: Did the answer refuse to call the day empty, and name which axis still holds evidence?

cases.title: A day explained by timelog and journal, with no artifact residue, stays explainable
cases.why: The second timeline golden day: timelog and journal explain it while depth-2/3 artifacts are silent. andenken's honest answer may be thin; what it must not do is manufacture a coordinate from a similarity score.

ownership.timeline: Owns the day's coordinates and that timelog/journal evidence exists.
ownership.andenken: Grades recoverable session/md anchors in the window, or an honest miss. Never asserts the date from a score.
ownership.harness: Grades whether the day becomes readable from the combined axes.

probes.windowNote: KST 2026-07-11 00:00–24:00 expressed as UTC. Stored-signal scan — API 0.

cases.humanPrompt: Does the thin result read as an honest limit of this axis rather than as an absence of life?
cases.harnessGrades: Did the answer carry the lived day without inventing artifacts that do not exist?
